rows.why: No item asks what a first hidden-tests pass releases or what the default share is. Item 1 is about rounding, item 3 about a second pass and item 7 about which shares are valid.

Item 1 asks how an uneven share is rounded. The pick floors with BigInt division and gives UAT the remainder: 999 at 7500 bps gives 749 and 250, which add up to the bounty, and BigInt keeps it exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. The ran call (101 → 75/26) shows the same floor-and-remainder behaviour.

No item asks what a first UAT approval does after the share was released. Item 4 covers a repeated UAT approval, item 2 covers UAT before the tests pass, and item 12 asks how status is calculated from stored sums, which is not the release itself.
Item 9 asks what happens when the hidden tests fail. The ran call shows no write for the failure event and a returned status of 'locked' with releases [].
Item 2 asks about UAT approval before the hidden tests pass. The pick throws 'the hidden tests have not passed' and records nothing, which is what the scenario expects.

Item 5 asks what the events do when the bounty is 0. The ran call records releases of amount 0 for hidden-tests and uat, but the scenario says no release is ever recorded. Only the 'pro bono' status matches.

Item 3 asks what happens when the hidden tests pass again after the release was made. The ran call uses a different event id and shows only one set (from the first pass) and the existing state returned. That matches the scenario's 'records nothing either' clause, and a same-id repeat falls under the same no-op.

Item 10 asks how concurrent duplicate events on one store are handled. The pick runs events one at a time per store, and the ran call with a delayed get shows two simultaneous hidden-tests-passed events producing sets: 1. Because events are serialised, the different-id and uat cases are also handled once.
Item 11 asks about store failures. The ran call shows set rejecting with 'boom', which propagates, stored stays undefined, and retrying the same event then succeeds with the hidden-tests release.
